title: PV Digital Twin, Tutorial 6: Limits and trust
label: Tutorial 6  ·  Limits and trust

beats.say: Five and ten percent are defaults, not laws. Set them too tight, and healthy days raise alarms. Set them too loose, and real faults slip through.
beats.visual: A horizontal deviation axis with a healthy cloud of dots near zero and a fault cluster at -30. Limits drawn as pairs of lines; cue 'tight' lines at +/-1 cutting through the healthy cloud (olive 'false alarms'); cue 'loose' lines at +/-40 leaving the fault cluster inside (olive 'missed fault').

beats.say: The tool can derive limits from a healthy day: the mean deviation plus two standard deviations for the warning, and plus three for the abnormal limit.
beats.visual: Histogram of the healthy daylight deviation from pvdata.day() (bins 0.25 % wide). Cue 'mean' a line at the mean; cue 'two' a line at mean + 2 sigma; cue 'three' a line at mean + 3 sigma.

beats.say: On the bundled day, that makes a warning limit of only about one point two percent, and about four percent of healthy daylight samples would exceed it.
beats.visual: Highlight the right tail of the histogram beyond the warning line; pill 'warning limit 1.2 %' and 'about 4 % of healthy samples above it'. Cue 'one' and 'four'.
beats.cap: On the bundled day, that makes a warning limit of only about 1.2%, and about 4% of healthy daylight samples would exceed it.

beats.say: The healthy deviation is not a neat bell shape, so those formulas are too tight here. Check derived limits before you trust them.
beats.visual: Callout 'TRAP' with 'Derived limits can raise false alarms: check them'. Cue 'trust'.

beats.say: Validation runs one healthy day and one day for each of the five faults, and scores the twin against what it knows is true.
beats.visual: Six small day-curve thumbnails: one healthy and five with a fault marker, appearing on cues 'healthy' and 'five'; a score pill 'Run validation'.

beats.say: Open Analysis, press the simulation button, then run validation. It takes a few seconds, and the app stays usable.
beats.visual: Show shot('simple_14_analysis_empty.png', width=10); box the SIMULATION button (top right) on cue 'simulation' and 'Run validation' on cue 'run'.

beats.say: On healthy data the error is tiny: M A E zero point two four watts, R M S E zero point three five, and M A P E zero point four seven percent. The baseline offset, the healthy day's average deviation, is minus zero point zero five percent.
beats.visual: Show shot('simple_15_analysis_results.png', width=10.5) with a box round the 'Accuracy on healthy data' card. Cue 'M', 'R', 'zero', then 'baseline' boxes the Baseline offset tile.
beats.cap: On healthy data the error is tiny: MAE 0.24 watts, RMSE 0.35, and MAPE 0.47%. The baseline offset, the healthy day's average deviation, is minus 0.05%.

beats.say: All five faults are detected, with a delay of zero seconds, and there are no false alarms at the default limits. Each fault also shows its mean deviation: about minus thirty one percent for partial shading, and about minus fourteen for sensor drift.
beats.visual: Box the 'Fault detection' card, then the 'Each fault' table, then its 'Mean deviation' column. Cue 'detected', 'delay', 'false', 'mean'.

beats.say: The last table counts what was true against what the twin said: every healthy sample read normal, and every fault sample read abnormal.
beats.visual: Box the 'Twin against truth' table (3210 and 300 green cells). Cue 'healthy', 'fault'.

scenes.title: What the scores do not say

beats.say: Read these scores with care. Each fault is injected as a sudden step for one hour, so the twin notices at once, and the scores come out perfect.
beats.visual: Draw a step function (fault step) next to a gradual ramp. Cue 'step' draw the step, label 'validation'; cue 'perfect' a pill '100 %'.

beats.say: Real faults arrive gradually, and would score lower.
beats.visual: Draw the gradual ramp in olive with label 'real faults'. Cue 'gradually'.

beats.say: And the plant and the twin are the same kind of model. So the accuracy shows how well the twin matches the simulation, not how it would do on a real module.
beats.visual: Two identical block icons 'plant' and 'twin' with an equals sign and a callout 'The same model family'. Cue 'same'.

beats.say: That is why the dataset route matters: it is how you test the twin against real measurements.
beats.visual: Arrow from a real-panel icon through 'dataset' into the twin. Cue 'dataset'.

beats.say: You now know the whole path. The sun and temperature set what a healthy module should make. The twin predicts it. The deviation measures the gap, and the limits turn it into a state.
beats.visual: A single horizontal flow diagram revealed in order on cues 'sun', 'twin', 'deviation', 'limits': [sun, temperature] -> [twin] -> [deviation] -> [state].

beats.say: Try it yourself. Inject each fault and read its fingerprint. Import a dataset. Compare the derived limits with the defaults. Then run validation, and read its warning.
beats.visual: Four checklist lines with boxes to tick, revealed on cues 'inject', 'import', 'compare', 'validation'.

beats.say: The manual has every button, and every file format, in detail. Thank you for watching.
beats.visual: End card: 'PV Digital Twin' title, subtitle 'the simple version manual covers every page', pill 'tutorials 1 to 6'. Cue 'manual'.
